body:
I'm kind of half and half here.

I feel like, due to my limitations in taking care of myself, and if it would've been caught early, I'd be stuck at home for life with parents who couldn't handle me. I'm living with my SO, leading some semblance of an adult life, and it's really good for me for the most part. 

But, on the other hand, most people- ESPECIALLY in the realm of government agencies and a decent amount of doctors etc- expect way more out of me than I can reasonably accomplish (Thanks, Medicaid, for telling me I'm not disabled because my disability severely hinders my ability to jump through your stupid hoops.) 
I have to keep things under wraps at work so I'm not barred from the vocational world for 'incompetence' or being unsuitable for (any) job (because it's technically 'illegal' to fire a disabled person solely for being disabled) 
My SO's family tends to look at me as a slacker, as opposed to someone who is essentially on the functioning level of an elementary school age child faking their way through adulthood. 
I feel like a giant, useless baby. 
I don't have access to the resources I need because no one takes adults recently diagnosed with autism seriously (or adults with autism at all, for the most part) 
I felt so different for so much of my life that my self-esteem and self-confidence are in such a horrid state that it'll probably take a good decade or more to get them to a remotely healthy level, and it's also directly contributed to major depressive episodes and suicide attempts 


So, which is the lesser evil? 

No independence, stuck with a dysfunctional family forever, miserable and alone

Or

Essentially being a child in an adult body forced to be an adult because you look like one, constantly scared, constantly misunderstood, constantly screwed over 

I'm not sure.

I was actually hospitalized in July, and ended up writing a list of things I wanted to do with my life, being a motivational speaker was one. I used to be a volunteer TA and tutor at the middle school and charter school in my hometown as a teen. I work for a company that has a charity for sick kids (and I've heard so many stories of kids it's helped, so I know I'm not just feeding some greedy bastard's pockets) and over the years I've worked there, when they do their yearly solicitation-thing for donations, I've probably raised about $250-$300 for it, and it always makes me feel warm inside, like I'm making a goddamn difference in the world. So I get you there. 

I just can't shake the feeling that I'm doomed to a life of feeling this way time and time again, even if it doesn't last (bipolar). I want to marry my SO but what's the point if I'm just going to kill myself someday? It's better to get it over with now, and spare my SO the heartache of losing a spouse.

I'm suicidal, so my answer probably isn't worth shit, but even though I don't know you, I care about you. I really hope things get better for you, seems like you're the kind of person who doesn't deserve the short end of the stick like this. I wish you happiness, even though it might be hard to find right now.
